Cámara Base is located on Half Moon Island in the South Shetland Islands. The Argentine station was established on April 1, 1953, under the name “Bahía Luna” and was renamed in 1955 in honor of naval officer Juan Cámara. After the 1959–1960 Antarctic campaign, the base became seasonal.

During summer, the station's researchers work in different parts of the island. Small buildings stand amid exposed rocks and patches of snow, close to Antarctic penguin habitats. Access to the station itself must be arranged separately: island walking rules exclude its buildings and operational grounds. Visits to the base depend on staff activity and expedition conditions.

Cambará do Sul lies on a highland plateau in the state of Rio Grande do Sul. Its surroundings feature open grasslands, rural roads, cool mists and araucaria trees with distinctive umbrella-shaped crowns. The town is a gateway to the canyons of southern Brazil.

The main natural attractions near Cambará do Sul are Itaimbezinho and Fortaleza. Trips to these canyons reveal how the level plateau drops away into deep, forested gorges. Visibility from the viewpoints depends on clouds and fog, so the experience can change considerably during the day. Allow time for driving and walking, and check access conditions before visiting.

Campo Grande is included in Brazilian itineraries as an arrival point before traveling on to the Pantanal. After landing, travelers transfer from here to their chosen hotel or nature lodge.

This city stop connects the flight with a journey through the Pantanal's rivers, plains and seasonally flooded areas. The precise onward route depends on the chosen itinerary.

In Devil's Canyon, the river journey takes you between towering vertical rock walls. Waterfalls cascade down the cliffs, while dense tropical vegetation thrives along the water's edge. From the boat, the cliffs can be seen rising to their full height.

This stretch forms part of the river route to Angel Falls. After the canyon, the journey continues to Ratoncito, where travelers set out on foot toward the Laime viewpoint.

At Canaima Lagoon, wide expanses of calm water sit beside powerful cascades. Palm trees grow along the shore, and the roar of waterfalls carries across the water. Travelers arrive here after a flight and return after river excursions.

Traditional curiara boat trips to Hacha and Sapo Falls begin at the lagoon. On a free day, you can stay by the shore or go kayaking. Available activities depend on the chosen itinerary and water conditions.
